hello.note: Two third tones in a row: nǐ is said with a rising tone. To elders or strangers: 您好 (nín hǎo).

goodbye.note: In casual speech people very often just say 拜拜 (bàibài), from English "bye-bye".

please.note: Goes before a verb: 请进 (qǐng jìn), "please come in". To ask a favour: 麻烦你 (máfan nǐ).

thank_you.note: The second 谢 is short and toneless. Warmer: 谢谢你 (xièxie nǐ).

youre_welcome.note: Also very common: 不用谢 (bú yòng xiè), "no need for thanks".

yes.note: Chinese often answers by echoing the verb: 有 (yǒu), 要 (yào). 对 (duì), "right", is also very common.

no.note: Or echo the verb: 不要 (bú yào), 没有 (méiyǒu). Declining an offer: 不用了 (bú yòng le).

sorry.note: For small slips, 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi) is lighter and more common.

excuse_me.note: Then ask with 请问 (qǐngwèn), "may I ask", followed by your question.

good_morning.note: Among friends and colleagues, simply 早 (zǎo)!

how_are_you.note: Not used with total strangers (你好 is enough). Casual: 最近怎么样？ (zuìjìn zěnmeyàng?)

im_fine.note: Also 还不错 (hái búcuò), "not bad". The textbook form is 我很好 (wǒ hěn hǎo).

whats_your_name.note: Politely asks the family name. To a child or peer: 你叫什么名字？ (nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?)

my_name_is.note: To give just your family name: 我姓… (wǒ xìng …).

nice_to_meet_you.note: To someone your age or younger: 很高兴认识你 (hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ).

where_from.note: 您是哪里人？ (nín shì nǎli rén?) asks which city or region someone comes from.

im_from.note: The country goes before 人: 我是英国人 (wǒ shì Yīngguó rén). Also 我来自… (wǒ láizì …).

speak_english.note: Put 请问 (qǐngwèn) in front to sound extra polite to a stranger.

dont_understand.note: Literally "I hear but can't follow". For something written: 我看不懂 (wǒ kàn bu dǒng).

speak_slowly.note: Softer: 您能说慢一点吗？ (nín néng shuō màn yìdiǎn ma?)

where.note: In northern China: 在哪儿？ (zài nǎr?)

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, 您说什么？ (nín shuō shénme?) is softer than a bare 什么？

who.note: Also pronounced shuí, especially in careful speech.

how_much.note: Point at the item as you ask. 这个 is often pronounced zhèige.

where_bathroom.note: 厕所 (cèsuǒ) is the everyday word; 洗手间 is the more polite one.

can_you_help.roman: Nín néng bāng wǒ yíxià ma?
can_you_help.note: 一下 (yíxià), "for a moment", softens the request.

one.note: Said yāo in phone, room and bus numbers, so it is not confused with 七 (qī).

two.note: Before a measure word use 两 (liǎng): 两个 (liǎng ge), "two of them".

four.note: Often avoided as unlucky, because it sounds like 死 (sǐ), "death".

six.note: Hand sign: thumb and little finger out, the other fingers folded.

seven.note: Hand sign: fingertips of thumb, index and middle finger pinched together.

eight.note: Hand sign: thumb and index finger out, like an L. A lucky number.

nine.note: Hand sign: index finger crooked like a hook.

ten.note: Rising tone; don't mix it up with 四 (sì), four. Hand sign: crossed index fingers or a fist.

water.note: Restaurants often serve hot water. Bottled water: 矿泉水 (kuàngquánshuǐ).

tea.note: 红茶 (hóngchá), literally "red tea", is what English calls black tea. Green tea: 绿茶 (lǜchá).

menu_please.roman: Qǐng gěi wǒ kàn yíxià càidān
menu_please.note: In restaurants 麻烦 (máfan), "sorry to trouble you", often replaces 请: 麻烦给我看一下菜单.

bill_please.note: 服务员 (fúwùyuán) calls the waiter. 结账 (jiézhàng) is just as common, especially in the north.

no_meat.note: Also 我吃素 (wǒ chī sù), "I'm vegetarian". 肉 on its own often means pork.

enjoy_meal.note: Said by a host or waiter. Among friends: 慢慢吃！ (mànmàn chī!), "take your time and enjoy".

left.note: Turn left: 左转 (zuǒ zhuǎn) or 往左拐 (wǎng zuǒ guǎi).

right.note: Turn right: 右转 (yòu zhuǎn) or 往右拐 (wǎng yòu guǎi).

straight_ahead.note: Also 往前走 (wǎng qián zǒu), "go forward".

stop_here.note: 师傅 (shīfu), "master", is the usual way to address a driver. Northern: 在这儿 (zài zhèr).

hotel.note: Also 宾馆 (bīnguǎn). 饭店 (fàndiàn) can be either a hotel or a restaurant.

train_station.note: Big cities have several, e.g. 北京南站 (Běijīng Nánzhàn), Beijing South.

want_to_go.note: 我要去… (wǒ yào qù …) sounds more definite, e.g. to a taxi driver.

one_ticket.roman: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhāng piào
one_ticket.note: 张 (zhāng) is the measure word for flat things like tickets.

too_expensive.note: When bargaining, follow up with 能便宜点吗？ (néng piányi diǎn ma?)

id_like_this.note: Softer: 我想要这个 (wǒ xiǎng yào zhège).

pay_card.note: Most people pay by phone and ask 可以扫码吗？ (kěyǐ sǎomǎ ma?), "can I scan the code?"

open.note: Literally "doing business". The plain word for open is 开 (kāi).

closed.note: Also 暂停营业 (zàntíng yíngyè), "temporarily closed". The plain word for closed is 关 (guān).

later.note: Means "in a little while"; also 等会儿 (děnghuìr). Later on, in the future: 以后 (yǐhòu).

good_evening.note: Used less than in English; 你好 works at any time of day.

good_night.note: Only before bed or when parting late at night, never as a greeting.

see_you_later.note: For later the same day: 待会儿见 (dāihuìr jiàn).

call_police.note: The police number in mainland China is 110.

need_doctor.note: Ambulance: dial 120, or say 叫救护车 (jiào jiùhùchē), "call an ambulance".

hospital.note: In an emergency, go to the 急诊 (jízhěn) department.

allergic.note: E.g. 我对花生过敏 (wǒ duì huāshēng guòmǐn), "I'm allergic to peanuts".

be_careful.note: 注意安全 (zhùyì ānquán), "stay safe", is a caring thing to say when parting.

of_course.note: To a request: 当然可以 (dāngrán kěyǐ), "of course you can".

maybe.note: Also 也许 (yěxǔ) or 说不定 (shuōbudìng).

dont_know.note: Politer: 我不太清楚 (wǒ bú tài qīngchu), "I'm not too sure".

im_tired.note: 累 is tired from effort; sleepy is 困 (kùn): 我困了 (wǒ kùn le).

im_happy.note: Also 我很高兴 (wǒ hěn gāoxìng).

welcome.note: Hosts often double it: 欢迎欢迎！ (huānyíng huānyíng!) Shops greet you with 欢迎光临 (huānyíng guānglín).

congratulations.note: Also 祝贺你 (zhùhè nǐ). At Chinese New Year: 恭喜发财 (gōngxǐ fācái).

my_family.note: Often just 我家 (wǒ jiā), which also means "my home".

brother.note: Older brother. Younger: 弟弟 (dìdi). Brothers in general: 兄弟 (xiōngdì).

sister.note: Older sister. Younger: 妹妹 (mèimei). Sisters in general: 姐妹 (jiěmèi).

child.note: Son: 儿子 (érzi); daughter: 女儿 (nǚ'ér).

friend.note: Same for men and women. But 男朋友 (nán péngyou) and 女朋友 (nǚ péngyou) mean boyfriend and girlfriend.

this_is_my_friend.note: Same for a female friend. In speech the 的 is often dropped: 这是我朋友 (zhè shì wǒ péngyou).

are_you_married.note: Asked quite freely in China, especially by older people. Casual: 你结婚了吗？ (nǐ jiéhūn le ma?)

have_children.note: Also 您有小孩吗？ (nín yǒu xiǎohái ma?)

monday.note: Literally "week one": the days are numbered from Monday. Also 周一 (zhōuyī).

tuesday.note: Also 周二 (zhōu'èr), common in writing and timetables.

wednesday.note: Also 周三 (zhōusān). In the south 礼拜三 (lǐbàisān) is common too.

sunday.note: The one day without a number. Also 星期日 (xīngqīrì) and 周日 (zhōurì).

what_day.note: Answer: 今天星期五 (jīntiān xīngqīwǔ). For the date: 今天几号？ (jīntiān jǐ hào?)

next_week.note: Also 下周 (xiàzhōu). Last week: 上个星期 (shàng ge xīngqī).

eleven.note: Simply 10 + 1. 十一 is also the name of the National Day holiday on 1 October.

twelve.note: Months are numbered too: 十二月 (shí'èr yuè), December.

fifty.note: On sale signs, 五折 (wǔ zhé) means you pay half price.

hundred.note: Unlike 十, the 一 is always said. 200 is 两百 (liǎngbǎi) or 二百 (èrbǎi).

thousand.note: Big numbers count in ten-thousands: 一万 (yíwàn), 10,000; 两万 (liǎngwàn), 20,000.

how_old.note: To a child: 你几岁了？ (nǐ jǐ suì le?) To an older person: 您多大年纪了？ (nín duō dà niánjì le?)

years_old.note: Often with 今年 (jīnnián), "this year": 我今年二十岁 (wǒ jīnnián èrshí suì).

red.note: Lucky and festive, seen at weddings and New Year. 红包 (hóngbāo) is a red money envelope.

green.note: A 绿帽子 (lǜ màozi), green hat, implies a man's partner is cheating, so never give one.

yellow.note: Can also mean "pornographic": 黄色网站 (huángsè wǎngzhàn) are adult websites.

black.note: 黑 can also mean shady or illegal: 黑车 (hēichē) is an unlicensed taxi.

white.note: Traditionally the colour of mourning, worn at funerals.

what_colour.note: Shopping: 有别的颜色吗？ (yǒu bié de yánsè ma?), "do you have other colours?"

another_one.note: Use the right measure word: 再来一瓶 (zài lái yì píng), one more bottle; 再来一杯 (zài lái yì bēi), cup.

its_hot.note: As an exclamation: 好热啊！ (hǎo rè a!) Hot and muggy: 很闷热 (hěn mēnrè).

its_cold.note: As an exclamation: 好冷啊！ (hǎo lěng a!) Pleasantly cool: 凉快 (liángkuai).

its_raining.note: Literally "rain is falling". Snowing: 下雪了 (xià xuě le).

its_sunny.note: When the sun comes out: 出太阳了 (chū tàiyáng le).

its_windy.note: Literally "the wind is big". Also 刮风了 (guā fēng le), "the wind's picking up".

beautiful_day.note: Also 今天天气真不错 (jīntiān tiānqì zhēn búcuò).

umbrella.note: Often just 伞 (sǎn). Not a good gift: 伞 sounds like 散 (sàn), "to split up".

winter.note: Spring: 春天 (chūntiān); autumn: 秋天 (qiūtiān).

have_reservation.note: Also 我有预订 (wǒ yǒu yùdìng). Then give the name it's under: 我姓… (wǒ xìng …).

room.note: Twin room: 双人间 (shuāngrénjiān); room with a double bed: 大床房 (dàchuángfáng).

passport.note: Needed for hotels and train tickets in China, so keep it with you.

wifi_password.note: WiFi is written in Latin letters and said "wai-fai". Also 无线网 (wúxiànwǎng), "wireless network".

check_out_time.note: 退房 (tuìfáng), literally "return the room", is check-out. Check-in: 入住 (rùzhù).

map.note: In China people use 高德地图 (Gāodé Dìtú) or 百度地图 (Bǎidù Dìtú) on their phones.

bus.note: Also 公共汽车 (gōnggòng qìchē); 巴士 (bāshì) in the south. Long-distance coach: 大巴 (dàbā).

next_train.roman: Xià yì bān huǒchē jǐ diǎn kāi?
next_train.note: Literally "what time does the next train leave?" For the metro: 下一班地铁 (xià yì bān dìtiě).

is_this_seat_free.note: Literally "is anyone here?" If it's free, you'll hear 没人 (méi rén).

what_do_you_do.roman: Nín shì zuò shénme gōngzuò de?
what_do_you_do.note: Shorter: 您做什么工作？ (nín zuò shénme gōngzuò?)

i_work_in.note: For a place: 我在银行工作 (wǒ zài yínháng gōngzuò). For a field: 我做销售 (wǒ zuò xiāoshòu), "I do sales".

im_student.note: Same for men and women. University student: 大学生 (dàxuéshēng).

meeting.note: To have a meeting is 开会 (kāihuì): 我在开会 (wǒ zài kāihuì), "I'm in a meeting".

im_busy.note: Softer, to turn something down: 我最近有点忙 (wǒ zuìjìn yǒudiǎn máng).

day_off.note: "I'm off today": 我今天休息 (wǒ jīntiān xiūxi). To ask for time off: 请假 (qǐngjià).

lets_start.note: 吧 (ba) at the end turns it into a suggestion, like "let's".

good_job.note: Also 做得很好！ (zuò de hěn hǎo!) After hard work people also say 辛苦了 (xīnkǔ le).

table_for_two.note: The usual answer when staff ask 几位？ (jǐ wèi?), "how many?" Also 两个人 (liǎng ge rén).

what_recommend.note: Or ask for the house special: 你们的招牌菜是什么？ (nǐmen de zhāopáicài shì shénme?)

not_spicy.note: If you can take a little heat: 微辣 (wēi là), "mildly spicy".

vegetarian_food.note: Vegetable dishes on a menu: 素菜 (sùcài), but they may still be cooked with meat stock or lard.

more_water.note: Water is often served hot. Cold: 冰水 (bīngshuǐ); room temperature: 常温的 (chángwēn de).

no_sugar.note: Bubble tea shops ask about sweetness: 无糖 (wú táng) is no sugar, 半糖 (bàn táng) half.

im_full.note: The polite way to refuse more food. Hosts often insist, so expect to say it more than once.

takeaway.note: Staff ask 堂食还是带走？ (tángshí háishi dàizǒu?), "eat in or take away?" Also 打包 (dǎbāo), used for leftovers too.

it_was_delicious.note: Chinese has no past tense; context does the work. To a host: 您做的菜太好吃了 (nín zuò de cài tài hǎochī le).

keep_change.note: Literally "no need to give change". Tipping isn't customary in China; mostly heard in taxis.

stomach.note: The everyday word for belly. The organ itself: 胃 (wèi). Stomach ache: 肚子疼 (dùzi téng).

head_hurts.note: Also 我头痛 (wǒ tóutòng). 疼 and 痛 both mean "hurt"; 疼 is more colloquial.

have_fever.note: A cold is 感冒 (gǎnmào): 我感冒了 (wǒ gǎnmào le), "I've caught a cold".

medicine.note: To take medicine is 吃药 (chī yào), literally "eat medicine".

call_ambulance.note: The ambulance number in mainland China is 120.

dentist.note: In a hospital, the dental department is 口腔科 (kǒuqiāngkē).

need_rest.note: More casual: 我想休息一下 (wǒ xiǎng xiūxi yíxià), "I'd like a little rest".

feel_better.note: Also 我感觉好多了 (wǒ gǎnjué hǎo duō le).

get_well.note: To an elder: 祝您早日康复 (zhù nín zǎorì kāngfù). Casual: 快点好起来！ (kuài diǎn hǎo qǐlai!)

lets_meet.note: Often heard but vague: 改天聚聚吧 (gǎitiān jùju ba), "let's get together sometime".

are_you_free.note: 空 here is kòng, "free time" (kōng means "empty"). To a friend use 你 (nǐ).

call_me.note: Friendlier: 给我打个电话吧 (gěi wǒ dǎ ge diànhuà ba). Many people prefer a WeChat message.

your_number.roman: Nín de diànhuà hàomǎ shì duōshao?
your_number.note: Numbers are read digit by digit, 1 as yāo. Often people swap WeChat: 加个微信吧 (jiā ge Wēixìn ba).

see_you_soon.note: Literally "see you next time". Also 改天见 (gǎitiān jiàn). Later today: 一会儿见 (yíhuìr jiàn).

have_nice_day.note: Mostly heard from service staff. Before a weekend: 周末愉快！ (zhōumò yúkuài!)

good_luck.note: Before an exam or a big task, say 加油！ (jiāyóu!), literally "add fuel".

thanks_a_lot.note: Warmer in speech: 太谢谢你了！ (tài xièxie nǐ le!) Also 多谢 (duōxiè).

miss_you.note: Warm and casual: 好想你！ (hǎo xiǎng nǐ!) 想 also means "to think" and "to want".
